title: TOI-682 b timing variations have an 822-day period and the transit shape shows an eccentric orbit, but near-resonant perturbers from 2.3 to 27 days fit TESS and TFOP times from 2019 to 2026
abstract: A prior campaign study found large transit timing variations (TTVs) of the sub-Neptune TOI-682 b (P = 6.84 d) in TESS data and proposed the radial-velocity (RV) planet c (P = 16.134 d, unrefereed poster) as their cause. We measured 20 TESS 2-minute transit times (2019-2026) and 3 ground-based TFOP transit times (2020, 2022, 2023) that pass fixed quality rules. A clock check with other planets in the same sectors gives offsets below 0.11 min. One sinusoid with a period of 822 +/- 17 d and a 22.7-min semi-amplitude fits all 23 times (chi-square 21.4, 18 degrees of freedom; linear ephemeris 1,013). From TESS alone, periods of 819 d and 1,490 d fit equally well; the 819-d fit predicts the independent ground times (chi-square 6.6 for 3 times), and the 1,490-d fit of the prior study misses the 2022 transit by 55 min. The transit is longer than a circular orbit permits: with the spectroscopic stellar density, g = 0.777 (+0.029/-0.045), so e_b >= 0.18 at 97.5 percent probability, independent of the RVs. We fitted coplanar two-planet REBOUND models with this shape constraint (369 local fits). If planet c causes the TTVs, its mean period must be 16.002 d or 15.958 d (near 7:3); the best fit has 8.1 Earth masses, near the RV minimum mass of 9.6. Near the reported period (16.10-16.17 d) the best chi-square found is 57.9, against 20.7. However, perturbers near 3:2, 5:3, 7:4, 2:1, 5:2, 3:1, 4:1, 1:2 and 1:3 fit about as well: 22 distinct solutions pass the 99 percent limit, with 0.09-20.5 Earth masses, RV semi-amplitudes of 0.03-4.5 m/s and e_b = 0.19-0.59. All are regular for 10,000 orbits. A TESS search finds no transiting inner planet larger than about 1.1-1.3 Earth radii in the interior windows, which does not exclude the small interior solutions. So the TTVs and the eccentricity of b are robust, but the perturber is not identified. 19 of the 22 solutions predict transits 20-30 min early in early 2027 and 10-23 min late in early 2028. Limitations: coplanar models, local fits on a likelihood with many modes (not a complete search), no access to the RVs, three ground transits with rules set after inspection, and a shape result that depends on the stellar density.

Bottom: residuals.

Best chi-square found (23 times plus the transit-shape term) for perturber-period windows with an 822-d super-period (left) and near the 7:3 commensurability (right). Red dashed line: 99 percent limit. Green line: reported RV period of planet c. Each point is the best of 4-12 local fits.
Predicted O - C of TOI-682 b from November 2026 to 2029 for the 22 accepted solutions. Orange: planet c near 7:3; grey: other exterior perturbers; purple: interior perturbers.
